### What we’re adding We’ll drop a **“Delete me”** button that: 1. **Shows a confirmation dialog** – to make sure the user meant to do it. 2. **Calls a secure serverless function** (`/api/delete-account`) to: * **Remove all rows** the user owns (posts, profile, uploads, etc.). * **Delete the Supabase Auth user** record so they can’t log back in. 3. **Shows a “Your account was deleted” page** and forces them out of the app. 4. **Keeps a small audit trail** (timestamp, user ID) in a read‑only admin table – useful if you ever need to prove the deletion. All of this happens on the server, so no secret keys are exposed in the browser code. --- ## Safety checklist for this feature | Feature | Safety part we build | |---------|----------------------| | Delete my account | *Confirmation step* (click‑to‑confirm).
*Server‑side deletion* (no user‑handled SQL).
*Delete Auth user* (supabase auth).
*Audit trail* (public‑only table).
*No accidental data leakage* – user can only delete their own rows. | --- ## One‑screen plan (Amber) ``` What we are building: a "Delete my account" button that removes the user’s data. Who uses it: any logged‑in user of the app. Risk level: Amber – personal data + Auth deletion. Day‑one features: 1. Delete button + confirmation dialog. 2. Server‑side deletion of user rows and Auth record. 3. Show account‑deleted page and log out. Information it stores: users' own data; audit trail (read‑only for admins). Login: yes (requires user to be logged in). Money: no. Built with: Next.js (React) for UI + Serverless API route, Supabase client on server. Steps: 1. Add a button in the profile page. 2. Create an API route `/api/delete-account`. 3. In that route: - Verify auth session. - Delete from all tables where `user_id == current_user.id`. - Call `supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(id)`. - Insert a row into `audit_deletions`. 4. Add a confirmation modal before calling the API. 5. After successful deletion, redirect to `/account-deleted` page and remove the JWT cookie. Safety: secrets in `.env` only on server, data locked to the owner, save point before each step. ``` Does this look right? Reply **yes** to proceed, or tell me what to change.
